grammar_notes.title: Colours & Describing Objects in Shona ('mutema')
grammar_notes.content: This passage uses colour vocabulary such as 'mutema'. Shona has three traditional core colour adjectives that change their prefix slightly to match the noun they describe: '-chena' (white/clean, e.g., 'ruvara ruchena' or 'shangu chena'), '-tema / nhema' (black/dark, e.g., 'mota nhema' or 'ruvara rutema'), and '-tsvuku' (red/bright brown, e.g., 'mota tsvuku' or 'ruvara rutsvuku'). For other colours like green ('girinhi'), blue ('bhuruu'), or orange ('orenji'), speakers typically say 'ruvara rwe-' ('the colour of...') followed by the colour name, as in 'ruvara rwegirinhi' (green).
grammar_notes.rule: Core Colours: -chena (white), -tema / nhema (black), -tsvuku (red) | Phrase pattern: ruvara rwe-[colour] (e.g., ruvara rwegirinhi)

grammar_notes.title: Counting & Numbers in Shona ('maviri')
grammar_notes.content: In Shona, number words like 'maviri' always come AFTER the noun they count, and their starting prefix matches the noun's group! The basic number stems are: '-mwe' (1), '-viri' (2), '-tatu' (3), '-na' (4), and '-shanu' (5). For example, when counting people ('vanhu'), you use 'va-': 'munhu mumwe' (1 person), 'vanhu vaviri' (2 people), 'varume vana' (4 men). When counting 'ma-' plurals like 'maminitsi' (minutes) or 'mavara' (colours), you use 'ma-': 'madhongi maviri' (2 donkeys), 'mavara matatu' (3 colours), 'maminitsi mashanu' (5 minutes).
grammar_notes.rule: Noun + Number Stem (-mwe = 1, -viri = 2, -tatu = 3, -na = 4, -shanu = 5) -> vanhu vaviri (2 people), maminitsi mashanu (5 minutes)

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('Parutivi')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'Parutivi'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

cultural_notes.title: Homestead Garden Tools ('Maturusi') & Local Blacksmith Craftsmanship
cultural_notes.content: Every rural and suburban household in Zimbabwe keeps a set of sturdy hand tools—hoes ('mabadza'), rakes ('mahara'), digging forks ('mafoko'), and shovels ('mafoshoro')—fitted with carved hardwood handles ('mibato yemuti') to prepare vegetable beds and clear stony yard paths.

options: My parents live at the rural homestead in Masvingo.

lessons.title: Chidzidzo 100: Maruva ane ruvara rwegirinhi yakachenuruka akadyarwa...
lessons.shona_text: Maruva ane ruvara rwegirinhi yakachenuruka akadyarwa mugaba rine ruvara rwegirinhi yakachenuruka zvakare. Gaba iri rakagadzikwa pamusoro peuriri hwesimende uye pane cheni mbiri dziri kudarika neparitivi paro.
lessons.english_translation: Plants with pale green leaves are planted in a light-green pot. This pot is set upon a cement floor, and two chains pass right beside it.

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('yakachenuruka')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'yakachenuruka' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

cultural_notes.title: Veranda Container Gardening & Ornamental Plants in Zimbabwe
cultural_notes.content: Container gardening—planting ornamental foliage and flowers ('maruva') in painted pots and tins ('magaba') arranged along smooth cement verandas ('pamusoro peuriri hwesimende')—is a cherished tradition in Zimbabwean homes, bringing greenery right to the doorstep even during the dry season.

active_exercises.explanation: 'Hembe chena' = 'white shirt', 'ne-' = 'and', and 'shangu nhema' = 'black shoes'.

active_exercises.correct_answer: rwegirinhi
active_exercises.explanation: 'Ruvara rwegirinhi' expresses 'green colour' when describing fresh leaves ('mashizha').

active_exercises.prompt: Complete this future weather forecast: 'Mangwana zuva ______ zvakanaka.' (Tomorrow the sun will shine brightly.)
active_exercises.correct_answer: richabuda
active_exercises.explanation: 'Zuva' (sun) takes the prefix 'ri-' + future marker '-cha-' + '-buda' (come out/shine) -> 'richabuda'.
